issues.legal_issue: A decree entered after a new endowment-regulation law took effect in a scheme suit filed before that law does not become void merely because it was entered after the law took effect, where the Board did not timely seek to have it declared void.
material_facts: The scheme suit was filed before the endowment-regulation law took effect, and the decree was entered after it took effect.
The defendants objected to execution of the decree on the ground that it was void because it post-dated the law.
The Board did not challenge the decree within the time available after learning of the suit or proceeding.
issues.conclusion: The suit did not abate when the law took effect, and the decree was not void or unenforceable on the defendants’ objection; the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 55 of the Wakf Act preserves the maintainability of suits under Section 92 of the Code of Civil Procedure after the Act, subject to the Board’s consent for suits instituted after the Act by persons other than the Board. Under Section 57(1), the court must notify the Board in suits or proceedings relating to title to wakf property or a mutawalli’s right; under Section 57(3), absence of notice permits the decree or order to be declared void if the Board applies within one month of learning of the proceeding. Section 59 permits the Board to appear and plead as a party in proceedings concerning a wakf or wakf property. Together, these provisions mean that a suit instituted before the Act does not abate, and any failure to notify the Board does not make the decree void unless the Board timely seeks that result. No earlier cases are relied upon.

rule.if: scheme_suit_under_public_trust_procedure and suit_preceded_regulatory_change and decree_followed_regulatory_change and board_did_not_timely_seek_invalidation and appeal_from_execution_objection

predicates.scheme_suit_under_public_trust_procedure: The proceeding was a suit seeking a court-framed scheme for the administration of a public religious endowment.
predicates.suit_preceded_regulatory_change: The suit was instituted before the relevant endowment-regulation law took effect.
predicates.decree_followed_regulatory_change: The court entered the decree after the endowment-regulation law took effect.
predicates.board_did_not_timely_seek_invalidation: The endowment board did not apply to have the decree declared void within the time available after learning of the proceeding.
predicates.appeal_from_execution_objection: The appeal arose from an objection to execution of the decree, rather than from an appeal against the decree itself.

issues.definition: When a scheme suit predates a regulatory change, its decree postdates that change, the board does not timely seek invalidation, and the matter is an appeal from an execution objection, the decree remains enforceable.
